app.name: AlphaPai
app.description: AI-native investment research assistant and workstation (PaiWork, PaiMeeting) for professional investors, built by Shanghai-based Rabyte Technology.

observations.note: Company press release (PR Newswire, Hong Kong, Sept. 15, 2026) announcing a US$50M Series B: 'Today it serves more than 120,000 professional users across over 8,000 financial institutions and asset managers'. Dated to the Sept 15 release, where the figure first appears; the Nov 13, 2026 Hong Kong FinTech Week release (https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/alphapai-launches-its-ai-native-investment-research-platform-for-global-markets-at-hong-kong-fintech-week-302937786.html) repeats the same figure for the 'China-market product' and is not a new reading. No basis set: 'professional users' does not say monthly, weekly or registered (the boilerplate says 'has served', which may be cumulative). 'More than' makes it a floor. Both pages read with Tavily extract. App URL is the maker's official site (rabyte.cn lists Alpha派); no separate product domain was confirmed.

app.name: Mercor
app.description: AI data company whose network of domain experts builds evaluations and post-training data for frontier labs and enterprises.

observations.note: Co-founder and CEO Brendan Foody's own LinkedIn post announcing the $750M Series D at a $20B valuation: 'Mercor scaled from $1M to $3B in run-rate revenue in 27 months, the fastest in history to $3B.' Named company executive, first-hand. The page shows only relative times; dated to the Nov 10, 2026 Series D announcement date (Business Wire release of that date; search metadata dates the post Nov 10). The Business Wire release itself gives no revenue figure. No basis set: the post does not say gross or net (commentators argue it is gross billings; that is not company-stated). The 27-month and 6-month windows are not recorded as growth. Page read with Tavily extract (advanced).
